newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW- Granite seeks viewership rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- Granite seeks viewership rise.

text.p: Granite Broadcasting Corp Chief Executive Don Cornwell said Wednesday that the company would like to increase the number of television households it reaches to 10 percent by the end of 1998.

The company now reaches eight percent of the viewing households. Although a two percent increase does not sound like a big jump, Cornwell said it would take the acquisition of a single station in a large market, or four or five stations in a market roughly the size of Buffalo, N.Y.
"We just think it's imperative to get bigger," Cornwell said in an interview.
The company was founded in 1988 with two stations. It grew to four stations by 1990, when "we got into a credit-crunch period," and held off on acquiring other stations until 1993.
Since then, it has acquired seven more stations.

It went public in 1992, growing from a company with $30 million in annual revenues to $151 million in annual revenues. Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization have grown from $13 million to $70 million.

Cornwell said Granite still views local news as the staple of its crop of stations. About half of the revenues generated by its stations come from local news, which accounts for about 15 percent of the air time.
At the same time, Granite has been looking to the Internet as a way to promote its stable of stations.

In a deal with Yahoo! Inc, the online Internet guide features local news feeds from Granite stations. In exchange, the Granite stations are using information from the Internet provided by Yahoo! and telling viewers where to find more information about newscasts on the Internet.
"It will make our news more available in the market," Cornwell said.
"Most of our stations get any where from 2,000 to 5,000, 6,000 hits a day" on the Web page, he said. On big news days, such as Election Day, the pages register as many as 20,000 hits, Cornwell said.
